title: Raw cone-presheaf adjunction and lifting preservation
statement:
Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and its ordered last-vertex cone from [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], the Kan model structure, Kan fibrations and trivial Kan fibrations of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$, enlarging universes when necessary, and put $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $\mathcal P_S$ be the category of simplicial functors $D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and enriched natural transformations. An enriched natural transformation consists of maps at objects commuting with the simplicial action maps. This category has the projective model structure: weak equivalences are objectwise weak homotopy equivalences, fibrations are objectwise Kan fibrations, and cofibrations have the left lifting property against objectwise trivial Kan fibrations; factorizations are functorial. Its mapping simplicial set $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(F,G)$ has degree-$n$ simplices the enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. A projectively fibrant presheaf is one taking values in Kan complexes; projectively cofibrant means that its initial map is a projective cofibration.

For $a:X\to S$ put $T_a=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[S]$, with cone vertex $v$, and define $L_S(X)(s)=T_a(s,v)$, with action by precomposition. Define $U_S(F)\to S$ by declaring its degree-$n$ simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ to be enriched natural transformations $L_S(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to F$; simplex operators are restriction. These are an ordinary adjunction $L_S\dashv U_S$. The functor $L_S$ sends every degreewise monomorphism over $S$ to a projective cofibration. If $f:(X,a)\to(Y,b)$ induces a Dwyer--Kan equivalence on $\mathfrak C[S\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)]\to\mathfrak C[S\amalg_Y(Y\star\Delta^0)]$, then $L_S(f)$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. Here Dwyer--Kan means weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping simplicial sets and equivalence on the categories of their path components. These assertions make no assumption of a model structure on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ and no quasicategory assumption on $S$.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 construction and first two sentences of the proof of Theorem 2.2.1.2 (the adjunction and preservation assertions only, without Quillen equivalence), together with Proposition A.3.3.2 for enriched projective model existence. No Stacks tag states this result. HTT reading copy is in the sandbox; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] only for its assertion that the Kan model on simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] with that model category and with the small simplicial category $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its first paragraph gives the enriched projective model structure, objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and functorial factorizations. It gives the objectwise tensor and the enriched-end mapping simplicial set, whose degree-$n$ elements are precisely enriched maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. An object is fibrant exactly when its terminal map is objectwise a Kan fibration, that is, when every value is Kan. The asserted description of cofibrancy is the definition of the initial map being a projective cofibration. Neither an ordinary-category interpretation of $D$ nor local Kan mapping sets are used.

source.place: §A.3.3, Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.4; instantiated using the existing simplicial projective-model interface

proof.text: Write $A=\mathfrak C[S]$. For a presheaf $F:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ form its collage $E_F$: objects are those of $A$ and one new object $v$; old-to-old mapping sets are those of $A$, $E_F(s,v)=F(s)$, $E_F(v,s)=\varnothing$, and $E_F(v,v)=\Delta^0$. Composition with old arrows is the presheaf action. Its associativity and units are exactly the action axioms. The realization and enriched colimits exist by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] and [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. The presentation of $T_a$ as an enriched pushout leaves its old mapping sets equal to $A$, its reverse mapping sets empty and its $v$-endomorphisms equal to $\Delta^0$: the cone has no arrow leaving $v$ except its identity, so a composable path involving a new arrow cannot return to an old object. All other new paths go from an old object to $v$. Explicitly, its old-to-$v$ mapping set at $s$ is the degreewise quotient of $\coprod_{x\in X_0} A(s,a(x))\times\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0](x,v)$ by the relations $(a(g)\circ h,z)\sim(h,z\circ g)$ for $g\in\mathfrak C[X](x,y)$, $h\in A(s,a(x))$, and $z\in\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0](y,v)$ in the same degree. Faces and degeneracies preserve these relations because composition is simplicial; precomposition acts on $h$. A word containing a cone arrow has that arrow last, so these are all relations involving new arrows. Maps from this presentation to any simplicial category are exactly pairs of enriched functors from the two pushout factors agreeing on $\mathfrak C[X]$, which verifies the pushout universal property. Thus $T_a$ is the collage of its presheaf $s\mapsto T_a(s,v)$. An enriched functor $T_a\to E_F$ equal to the identity on $A$ and on $v$ is precisely a family of maps $T_a(s,v)\to F(s)$ commuting with precomposition, hence precisely an enriched natural map $L_S X\to F$. This is a strict bijection, natural in $X$ and $F$, with no Kan hypothesis.

source.place: §2.2.1, the correspondence description of M; agent expansion by the explicit collage presentation

proof.text: The simplex-colimit definition of $\mathfrak C$ in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] preserves colimits: a functor from $\mathfrak C[K]$ to any simplicial category $B$ is exactly a compatible family of functors from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ for every simplex of $K$. Such families are exactly maps $K\to N(B)$ for $N(B)_n=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathfrak C[\Delta^n],B)$; applying the mapping-out definition of a colimit proves preservation. An enriched map from $T_a$ to $E_F$ as in Step 2 is equivalently a compatible choice of such maps for the cone on every simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, all equal on $A$ and on the single vertex $v$. Indeed every mixed simplex of $X\star\Delta^0$ is a simplex of $X$ followed by vertices at $v$, and face and degeneracy compatibility is exactly the indicated compatibility on cone simplices. A compatible family of maps $L_S(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{a\sigma}S)\to F$ is in turn exactly a map $X\to U_S F$ over $S$: send $\sigma$ to that family member; for every $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ the equation is $\eta_{\sigma\circ\Delta(\alpha)}=\eta_\sigma\circ L_S(\Delta(\alpha))$, precisely the restriction defining $U_S$. This proves the natural bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(L_S X,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{/S}(X,U_S F)$. Its two constructions are inverse on every simplex, proving the adjunction and its identity laws. For $X=\varnothing$, the relative cone has only the fixed base $A$ and $v$, $L_S X$ is initial, and both sets in the bijection are singletons. The same mapping-out proof gives the canonical identification $T_a\cong\mathfrak C[S\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)]$, fixing $A$ and $v$.

source.place: §2.2.1, direct construction of Un and the adjunction; §2.2.2, simplex-colimit formula; agent expansion including the empty domain

proof.text: Use the generating class $I$ and its notation $I\text{-inj}$, $I\text{-cof}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. If $p:B\to C$ is $I$-injective, it is surjective on objects by the object generator, and each $B(b,b')\to C(pb,pb')$ has the right lifting property against every simplex boundary by the two-object generators. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] these local maps are trivial Kan fibrations, and so lift against every degreewise monomorphism. In particular $U(\partial B_m)\to U(B_m)$ has the left lifting property against every $I$-injective functor. The cube attachment in [lem-coef-rigidification-boundary-cube] and pushout closure of lifting classes [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] imply that $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is $I$-cofibrant for $n\geq1$; for $n=0$ it is the object generator itself. Every simplicial monomorphism is a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of boundary inclusions by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply the colimit preservation proved in Step 3. Coproducts of left-lifting maps have the same property by choosing one filler per summand and taking their coproduct; pushouts preserve it by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and continuous transfinite composites preserve it by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Therefore $\mathfrak C[j]$ is $I$-cofibrant for every simplicial monomorphism $j$. This argument uses no Joyal model structure or coherent-nerve equivalence.

source.place: §2.2.5, first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, with the boundary-cell and lifting-closure arguments expanded

proof.text: Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be over $S$ and let $p:F\to G$ be an objectwise trivial Kan fibration. A lifting square for $L_S i$ against $p$ becomes, by Step 2, compatible functors $T_X\to E_F$ and $T_Y\to E_G$ fixing $A$ and $v$. The induced $E_F\to E_G$ is $I$-injective: it fixes and hence surjects on objects, its old mapping maps and its $v$-endomorphism map are identities, its maps from $v$ to old objects are empty identities, and its maps from old objects to $v$ are precisely the trivial Kan fibrations $p_s$. These satisfy the boundary lifting tests by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the generators in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Put $P=Y\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)$; the map $j:P\hookrightarrow Y\star\Delta^0$ is a monomorphism, since in each simplicial degree it includes exactly the base simplices of $Y$, the cone vertex, and the mixed simplices whose initial part lies in $X$. The given square specifies a functor $\mathfrak C[P]\to E_F$ and a compatible functor $\mathfrak C[Y\star\Delta^0]\to E_G$. Step 4 gives a lift to $E_F$. Its restriction to $\mathfrak C[Y]$ is the prescribed map through $A$, since $Y\subseteq P$; its restriction to the cone vertex is the prescribed $v$. It therefore extends across the defining pushout to $T_Y\to E_F$ over $A$ and $v$, and recovers a filler $L_S Y\to F$. Thus $L_S i$ has the left lifting property against every objectwise trivial Kan fibration, which is exactly a projective cofibration in the model of Step 1. This also treats $X=\varnothing$ because $P$ still contains $v$.

source.place: §2.2.1, first sentence of the proof of Theorem 2.2.1.2; agent-written lifting proof with collages, expanding the preservation assertion

proof.text: Finally Step 3 identifies the functor in the relative-cone hypothesis with $T_X\to T_Y$, identically on $A$ and on the cone vertex. By the stated definition of Dwyer--Kan equivalence, its map on the mapping simplicial set of the particular pair $(s,v)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every object $s$ of $A$. These maps are exactly $(L_S f)(s):T_X(s,v)\to T_Y(s,v)$. Hence $L_S f$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. No preservation of a homotopy pushout, no essential-surjectivity inference, and no model structure on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ enter this argument.
